answer: The cobbler's shop keeps a wooden last for every customer, carved to that foot alone and shelved for life. A wander last bought from another shop fails the register: at the karst of the fitting the last must match the foot the shop measured, and a strange last pinches or slips. Carving a fake identity means bribing a cobbler, forging thirty years of fittings and paying 8,700 in fees, while the vault mark burned into each last is read at every repair, so a second customer claiming the same last is turned away.
